name: coconut
why: A Python-compiling functional language with pattern matching and pipelines; a curious dialect, though it is still Python underneath.

brief.what_it_is: Coconut is a functional programming language that compiles to Python. It takes Coconut source files (Python syntax plus extra features) and produces ordinary Python code that runs on the Python interpreter. The added syntax includes short lambdas (x -> x + 1), pipelines (|>, ..>), partial application (map$(.**2)), enhanced pattern matching, destructuring assignment, multidimensional array literals, lazy recursive iterators, parallel_map, tail call optimization, and algebraic data types via data. Because all valid Python is valid Coconut, existing Python code should carry over unchanged.
brief.why_it_exists: The author's framing is to let Python programmers use the tools of modern functional programming "in as Pythonic a way as possible", and to give code that runs the same across Python versions: the homepage says Coconut "can backport almost all modern Python features as far back as Python 2.6."
brief.how_it_works: Coconut is a source-to-source compiler: you write .coco code, and it is compiled into Python that runs on a standard Python interpreter. The README describes it as a variant of Python that adds new syntax on top of Python's syntax; it does not describe the compiler internals beyond that.

commands_seen.context: The only install command in the homepage and README; installs Coconut from PyPI, which the homepage presents as giving access to all of Coconut's features.

brief.install_notes: Install with pip install coconut (from PyPI). Brew's executables list includes coconut, coconut-run, coconut-py3, coconut-py3-run, coconut-py3.14 and -run, coconut-release and -run, coconut-v3 and -run, coconut-v3.2 and -run, and coconut-v3.2.0 and -run. No accounts, hardware or extra configuration were mentioned. The README does not give first-run steps beyond the tutorial link.
brief.standout: Coconut adds a lot of functional syntax (pipelines, partial application with $, point-free composition with ..>, data types with addpattern) while staying a superset of Python, so the output is plain Python. The homepage also claims that Python 3.10-style pattern matching is extended and backported to all supported Python versions.
brief.status: unknown. The README links to a releases page and to active Open Collective backer and sponsor sections, and the homepage links to a GitHub repo, but I did not see a release date, last commit date or version number in the fetched pages.
brief.caveats: The brew formula has no caveats. The 'all valid Python is valid Coconut' claim is the homepage's own framing; I did not verify it. The online interpreter linked from the README is hosted at a cs121-team-panda GitHub Pages address, not on coconut-lang.org. The README does not state a license or supported Python versions beyond the 2.6 backport claim. The executable list suggests many version-pinned wrappers, which I did not explain.
quotes: Since all valid Python is valid Coconut, using Coconut will only extend and enhance what you're already capable of in Python.
Coconut is a variant of Python that adds on top of Python syntax new features for simple, elegant, Pythonic functional programming.
Coconut can backport almost all modern Python features as far back as Python 2.6.

judge.reason: Coconut turns Python into a functional language with pipelines, pattern matching, algebraic data types, and tail-call optimization, making it an interesting compiler and language to explore.

entry.title: Coconut
entry.tldr: A functional language that compiles to plain Python, adding pipelines, pattern matching and short lambdas while staying a superset of Python.
entry.deeper_look:
Coconut is a source-to-source compiler. You write `.coco` files in Python plus extra syntax, and it produces ordinary Python that runs on a standard interpreter. The README calls it "a variant of Python that adds on top of Python syntax new features for simple, elegant, Pythonic functional programming."

The added syntax covers a lot of ground: short lambdas like `x -> x + 1`, pipelines with `|>`, composition with `..>`, partial application such as `map$(.**2)`, destructuring assignment, pattern matching, algebraic data types via `data`, lazy recursive iterators, `parallel_map`, tail call optimization and multidimensional array literals.

The author's stated aim is to let Python programmers use the tools of modern functional programming in as Pythonic a way as possible. The homepage also says Coconut "can backport almost all modern Python features as far back as Python 2.6", so the same source can target many Python versions. It claims that all valid Python is valid Coconut, so existing code should carry over, though that is the project's own framing.

The idea underneath is that a language can be a thin layer over another one. Because the output is readable Python, you can see exactly what each pipeline or pattern match turns into, which makes it a way into how functional features map onto a language that was not designed for them.
entry.install:
brew install coconut
# The README's own install route is: pip install coconut

entry.whats_unique: It extends Python with pipelines, pattern matching and partial application without leaving the Python ecosystem, since the output is plain Python. It also backports newer Python features to older versions.
entry.caveats: Release dates and current maintenance status were not visible in the sources, and the many version-pinned executables installed by brew are unexplained.
